grounding.states: short-term melatonin use appears safe for most people
grounding.from: The NIH says short-term melatonin use appears safe for most people
information on long-term safety is lacking

grounding.states: low doses are typically safe and well tolerated, taken for the shortest time
grounding.from: UC Davis Health (Feb 2025) says melatonin is typically safe and well tolerated at low doses, taken appropriately for the shortest time

grounding.states: short-term means one to two months (UC Davis)
grounding.from: UC Davis defines short-term as one to two months.

grounding.states: GoodRx advises against daily use for more than a week or two at a time
grounding.from: GoodRx advises against taking it daily for more than a week or two at a time.

grounding.states: dose advice varies: 3 to 5 mg (GoodRx) versus 0.3 to 1 mg (Yale New Haven)
grounding.from: Sources disagree on the right dose.

grounding.states: a year or more of use in chronic insomnia was linked to higher heart failure rates in a preliminary study, not peer-reviewed, that cannot prove cause
grounding.from: An American Heart Association abstract was presented in November 2025. It linked melatonin use of a year or more in people with chronic insomnia to higher rates of heart failure diagnosis... The AHA says the study cannot prove cause and effect. The AHA also says the findings are preliminary because abstracts at its meetings are not peer-reviewed.

grounding.states: some experts think poor sleep may explain the results
grounding.from: Scientific American reports that some experts think the results may reflect the effects of poor sleep rather than melatonin.

grounding.states: older adults should use melatonin with caution because of possible fracture risk
grounding.from: The PMC review says the possible fracture risk is a reason to use melatonin with caution in older adults and in people with previous low-impact fractures.

grounding.states: check with a healthcare team before starting, especially with other medications
grounding.from: GoodRx says melatonin has side effects and drug interactions. It suggests checking with a healthcare team before starting.

value.answer: Short-term, yes: for most adults it's generally considered safe, and low doses are the usual advice. Sources don't agree on the details, though. UC Davis calls short-term one to two months, GoodRx says a week or two of daily use at a time, and the dose advice ranges from about 0.3 to 1 mg up to 3 to 5 mg. Long-term use is the open question. A preliminary heart failure link came out of a heart association meeting in November 2025, but it isn't peer-reviewed, can't show cause, and some experts think poor sleep is the real factor. Older adults should be careful because of fracture risk, and it's worth checking with a healthcare team before starting, especially if you take other meds.
